items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: Johnny Griffin were my father’s students. So you’re listening to them and they come in...

ctx.x: Did you, at that time, start to think that’s one of the things I would like to do. What he’s doing? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

The performance part of it yes, and the ensemble parts of it and working that hard was, but like the rest of school there were other ambitions that I had. There were other tastes that I had that I couldn’t satisfy simply within that one type of music. You know I had grown up around Chicago jazz all my life. My father was a saxophone player and a teacher, had notable students among them: Gene Ammons and Johnny Griffin. And these were kinds of people that I was used to being around and growing up with.
Your father taught those two players?
